title: Output preservation in one clocked attempt
statement: Let $S$ be a deterministic machine and $A$ a nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. For any work-tape contents and head positions for $S$, and any Boolean choice word $w$ of length $m+1$, the host machine with looping disabled, run from the corresponding run configuration based on $A$’s initial configuration with the yard tape head at $0$, halts; moreover, for every Boolean $v$, its output is exactly $[v]$ if and only if the run of $A$ under the first $m$ bits of $w$ halts and has output exactly $[v]$.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a deterministic machine over Boolean symbols
$A$ is a nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols
$sT$ assigns Boolean tape contents to each work-tape cell of $S$
$sP$ assigns an integer head position to each work tape of $S$
$w$ is a Boolean word with length $m+1$
